Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Summary of Labour Party Manifesto 2001 (within 500 words)

Core vision
- Build on foundations since 1997 to deliver a second-term programme of national renewal: sustained economic stability, world-class public services through investment and reform, a modern welfare state based on rights and responsibilities, safer communities, and a confident, engaged Britain abroad.
- Guiding principle: put power, wealth and opportunity in the hands of the many, not the few.

Five pledges for the next five years
- Economic: Keep mortgages and inflation low with sound public finances; avoid boom and bust.
- Schools: 10,000 extra teachers and higher standards in secondary education.
- Health: 20,000 extra nurses and 10,000 extra doctors in a reformed NHS; improve care free at the point of use.
- Crime: 6,000 extra police recruits to reach record police numbers; tackle drugs and crime.
- Families: Retain the winter fuel payment; raise the minimum wage to £4.20.

Record since 1997 (basis for second term)
- Typical mortgage costs £1,200 less than under the Conservatives; lowest inflation for 30 years.
- Best-ever primary school results; literacy and numeracy reforms embedded.
- 17,000 extra nurses; waiting lists and times reduced.
- Crime down 10% (British Crime Survey).
- One million more people in work; New Deal helped youth and long-term unemployed; new Children’s Tax Credit introduced.
- Targeted support raised poorest pensioners’ incomes (minimum income £100 single/£154 couple).
- Devolution delivered; constructive engagement in Europe; leadership on aid, debt relief and development.

Ten goals for 2010
- Long-term economic stability and rising living standards.
- Expanded higher education alongside higher secondary standards.
- A healthier nation with fast, free treatment.
- Full employment in every region.
- Opportunity for all children; security for all pensioners.
- A modern criminal justice system.
- Strong, accountable local government.
- British leadership in a reformed, enlarged EU.
- Action on global poverty and climate change.

Policy approach for the second term
- Economy: Skills, infrastructure and technology to boost productivity; major adult basic-skills drive.
- Public services: Empower professionals; invest and reform schools, NHS, culture and sport to raise quality and access.
- Welfare: Restructure benefits around work; transform support for children and families; improve cash and services for pensioners.
- Communities and crime: Reform criminal justice end-to-end to catch, punish and rehabilitate; tackle causes of crime; empower local communities with resources and responsibility.
- Foreign policy: Engage fully in Europe; support EU enlargement and reform; British people to have final say on joining the euro; lead on environment and global poverty.
- Method: An active, enabling state working in partnership with private and voluntary sectors.

Choice presented
- Labour: Stability, investment, engagement, and inclusion.
- Conservatives: Risk of 1980s-style boom and bust, cuts and privatisation, and European isolation (including opposition to the Nice Treaty and threats to UK stability via two classes of MP).

Tone
- Optimistic call to continue modernisation for hard-working families so all children have an equal chance to share in Britain’s opportunities and wealth.
